h1: Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park — 5-Star Marriott Next to Benjasiri Park in Bangkok's Japanese Quarter
intro: On Sukhumvit Soi 24, a quiet side street that expats and long-stay travellers have trusted for decades, sits one of Bangkok's most capable serviced apartment properties — Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park Bangkok. Rooms look out over the green canopy of Benjasiri Park, and the EM District (Emporium, EmQuartier, EmSphere) sits just a short walk away, alongside a stretch of authentic Japanese restaurants that give this corner of mid-Sukhumvit its unmistakable neighbourhood feel. With 300 units featuring fully equipped kitchens, a sports complex rivalling a private club, and a complimentary shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong, this is less hotel, more home — backed by Marriott's reliability. From approx. ฿4,200/night. Score: 9.1 from 408 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Sukhumvit Soi 24 is the kind of street that doesn't shout. No rooftop bars visible from the footpath, no crowds spilling out of nightclubs — just a leafy residential road that happens to put you within walking distance of some of Bangkok's best shopping and a remarkable concentration of Japanese restaurants. Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park has occupied this address for years, and the returning guests — Japanese families, corporate expats on extended assignments, and Bangkok regulars who've tried newer properties and come back — are the clearest endorsement the place has.

Every unit comes with a kitchen properly equipped for real cooking: electric hob, microwave, refrigerator, dishwasher, and a washer-dryer combo. This matters far more than it sounds after a week away from home. For families, it means breakfast doesn't have to be a hotel transaction, and for long-stay guests, it cuts daily costs substantially. Unit sizes run from 45-sq-m studios to 180-sq-m three-bedroom apartments — there's a size for every group configuration.

"Having a full kitchen made all the difference for our family. We'd do breakfast in the apartment, head out, and come back to find housekeeping had everything spotless. The kids loved the pool and the children's club — we barely left the property on rest days."

The sports and recreation facilities are what separate this property from standard hotels at similar price points. Beyond the outdoor pool and children's pool, the complex offers tennis courts, badminton courts, a squash court, a billiards room, table tennis, and a rooftop golf simulator — plus a 24-hour fitness center. For a family or a corporate group on a week-long stay, that's a private club included in the room rate.

The location anchors everything. Benjasiri Park borders the property directly — Bangkok's compact answer to a neighbourhood green, where guests walk, jog and cycle without setting foot in traffic. Emporium is roughly 8 minutes on foot, EmQuartier another 2 minutes beyond that. The complimentary shuttle departs every 30 minutes for BTS Phrom Phong, removing the 870-metre walk in Bangkok's heat as a daily problem. The Japanese town of mid-Sukhumvit surrounds you: authentic ramen shops, izakayas, convenience stores stocked with imported goods — the kind of neighbourhood infrastructure that makes long stays feel genuinely sustainable.

Staff quality stands out across most reviews: Booking.com's staff score reaches 9.6, and individual team members are cited by name in multiple reviews — a reliable sign of service that goes beyond script. Breakfast at Bistro M offers a multi-cuisine buffet spanning Japanese, Thai, American, and vegetarian options, with a variety that handles a diverse guest base well. The caveat, flagged honestly across several platforms, is that service consistency can vary by shift — some guests encountered noticeably less warmth at the front desk on certain occasions.

The building carries its age visibly. Some units and bathrooms show finishes that belong to an earlier era of interior design, and while cleanliness is consistently praised, travellers expecting the freshness of a newly opened property may find certain corners feel dated. The shuttle also occasionally runs behind schedule in peak hours — factor in buffer time if you have a fixed appointment. None of this knocks the overall experience significantly: a 9.1 aggregate score across 408 reviews speaks for itself, and for the profile of traveller this property suits best, the combination of apartment living standards with five-star facilities in this particular neighbourhood is hard to replicate anywhere nearby.

highlights.title: Full Kitchen in Every Unit
highlights.text: Every apartment comes with hob, microwave, fridge, dishwasher and washer-dryer. Cook, do laundry, settle in — this genuinely functions as a home.

highlights.title: Benjasiri Park on the Doorstep
highlights.text: Bangkok's Phrom Phong green lung is right outside. Jog, walk or cycle first thing without a single traffic light. EM District is 8 minutes on foot.

highlights.title: Private-Club Sports Complex
highlights.text: Tennis, badminton, squash, billiards, rooftop golf simulator, 24-hr gym, kids club and children's pool — all included with your stay.

honestSummary: Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park is a strong choice for families, corporate long-stayers and anyone who wants apartment-living standards with five-star support in a genuinely pleasant Bangkok neighbourhood. The sports facilities and park access are exceptional for the area. The property's age shows in spots, and service consistency could be sharper — but the numbers across 400+ reviews confirm this delivers on what it promises.
honestChecks: If you want a freshly designed, contemporary room — the building carries its age and some units feel dated → compare with newer properties in the same neighbourhood before booking
If you have a tight schedule relying on public transport — the shuttle occasionally runs behind; it's 870m to BTS on foot in Bangkok heat → build in extra time or budget for taxis during peak hours

If you're only staying 1–2 nights and won't use the kitchen — the per-night rate may be less competitive versus hotel-only options nearby → this property pays off most from 3 nights upward, when the apartment format earns its keep

tips.title: Request a Benjasiri Park-facing unit
tips.body: The park view is the property's finest outlook — trees and green in the morning light rather than a concrete soi. Request it at booking; it makes a real difference to the feel of the stay.

tips.title: Use the free shuttle, not your legs, in the heat
tips.body: The complimentary shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong and Emporium runs every 30 minutes. During morning and evening rush, it can run late — add buffer time before any fixed appointment.

tips.title: Make the kitchen earn its keep
tips.body: Tops Supermarket is nearby, authentic Japanese grocers are within walking distance, and Fuji Restaurant is moments away. Buy ingredients and cook occasionally — on a long stay, it cuts costs and makes the apartment feel like home.

tips.title: Weekly and monthly rates are better value
tips.body: Serviced apartments typically offer better per-night pricing on extended bookings. Contact the hotel directly or compare multi-week rates on the booking platforms — the gap is worth checking before you commit.

faqTitle: FAQ — Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park and how do I get to BTS?
faq.a: The property is at 90 Sukhumvit Soi 24, Khlong Toei, Bangkok 10110. BTS Phrom Phong is 870 metres away — about 12 minutes on foot. A complimentary shuttle bus runs every 30 minutes directly to the BTS station and Emporium mall. The hotel sits next to Benjasiri Park and is within walking distance of the EM District (Emporium, EmQuartier, EmSphere).

faq.q: What are the prices and what apartment types are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿4,200/night for a 45-sq-m Executive King Studio. Options scale up to 1 Bedroom Family Suites (65 sq m), 2 Bedroom Apartments (130 sq m), and 3 Bedroom Apartments (180 sq m). All units include a fully equipped kitchen with washer-dryer. Prices vary by dates and platform.

faq.q: Who is Marriott Executive Apartments Sukhumvit Park best suited for?
faq.a: This property suits families on extended stays, corporate travellers on multi-week assignments, and anyone who needs apartment functionality with five-star hotel support. The Phrom Phong neighbourhood is mid-Sukhumvit — calm, well-serviced and central. It's less suited to short one-night stays where the kitchen and apartment format don't have time to pay off.

faq.q: What kitchen appliances are included in the apartments?
faq.a: Every unit is furnished with an electric hob, microwave, refrigerator, dishwasher, and washer-dryer combo, plus basic cookware and utensils. A Tops Supermarket and several Japanese grocery shops are nearby, making self-catering practical and worthwhile on longer stays.

faq.q: What sport and wellness facilities does the hotel offer?
faq.a: The on-site complex includes an outdoor pool, children's pool, 24-hour fitness center, tennis courts, badminton courts, a squash court, a billiards room, table tennis, a rooftop golf simulator, and a dedicated kids club. For a long-stay or family visit, this is a strong suite of amenities that removes the need to seek out a separate gym or sports club.
